definitions.explanation: The physical quality of being heavy. The felt sense of heaviness in an object.
The quality of being important, serious, or carrying authority. Used for words, decisions, positions, and responsibilities.

examples.japanese: この{石|いし}はかなりの{重|おも}みがある。
examples.english: This stone has quite a bit of weight.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんを{抱|だ}くと、{命|いのち}の{重|おも}みを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: When I hold a baby, I feel the weight of life.

examples.japanese: ずっしりとした{重|おも}みのある{鉄|てつ}の{鍋|なべ}は{熱|ねつ}が{均一|きんいつ}に{伝|つた}わる。
examples.english: A solid, heavy iron pot distributes heat evenly.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}の{言葉|ことば}には{重|おも}みがある。
{経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}むことで、{発言|はつげん}に{重|おも}みが{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: As you gain experience, your statements gain gravitas.

examples.japanese: {責任|せきにん}の{重|おも}みに{耐|た}えかねて、{辞任|じにん}を{決意|けつい}した。
examples.english: Unable to bear the weight of responsibility, he decided to resign.

notes:
The nominal form of {重|おも}い (heavy), expressing heaviness as a quality or abstract concept.

SENSE 1 (physical):
Describes the felt heaviness of an object.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (physical):
- {重|おも}みがある (to have weight)
- ずっしりとした{重|おも}み (solid weight)

SENSE 2 (figurative):
Describes the significance, authority, or gravity that something carries.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (figurative):
- {言葉|ことば}の{重|おも}み (the weight of words)
- {責任|せきにん}の{重|おも}み (the weight of responsibility)
- {重|おも}みを{増|ま}す (to gain significance)
- {重|おも}みのある{発言|はつげん} (a weighty statement)
